heroCopy: Turn intent into a bounded Harness–Graph–Loop Blueprint. Validate it. Ask a human. Only then generate the system.
whyTitle: More agents are not a design.
whyCopy: Reliability comes from explicit boundaries: what enters, what may act, what returns, what proves success, and when the system stops.
journeyTitle: From a need to a system you can inspect.
journeyCopy: The Blueprint keeps design separate from execution, and keeps evidence separate from conversation volume.
storyOne: Bound the intent. Write the Blueprint. Leave the toolbox closed.
storyTwo: Separate environment control, dependency routing, and local feedback.
storyThree: A human reviews the design before generation begins.
storyFour: Workers return compact results and evidence—not whole transcripts.
harnessCopy: Tools, permissions, context, budgets, state, evidence, cancellation, and provider boundaries.
graphCopy: Typed nodes, explicit edges, entry points, failure routes, fan-in, and independent review.
loopTitle: Make feedback change the next attempt.
loopCopy: Gather, act, verify, repair, persist, and stop—inside a finite budget.
contractTitle: A design artifact a human can reject.
contractCopy: The Blueprint is provider-neutral, machine-validatable, and unable to approve itself. Material changes return it to review.
p2Copy: Each phase receives only the capabilities it needs.
p3Copy: Unsupported runtimes remain future work, not badges.
p4Copy: A fresh agent can resume without reconstructing chat history.
startCopy: Ask the Skill to design first. It will choose the smallest justified shape, validate the contract, and stop at the human approval gate.
startPrompt: Use $harness-graph-loop-builder to design a reviewable HGL Blueprint for [my goal]. Do not build until I approve.
useCasesCopy: Code repair · data analysis · medical education · content production · compliance · dataset quality · product delivery
finalTitle: Build fewer systems. Trust the ones you build.
finalCopy: Provider-neutral by design. Codex-first in version one.
